question: Why are even vast preliminary rites rendered futile without proper worship and offerings to the guru?
premises: Proper worship of the guru brings ritual completeness.
Proper offerings to the guru are required as part of that worship.
Without these, all ritual efforts become fruitless.
inference: Therefore, even ten million preliminary rites are of no use if proper guru-worship and offerings are neglected.
uncertainties: The exact scope of 'sarvaṃ' (all rites or all results) is contextually inferred from the preceding verses.
plain_english: Otherwise, everything is fruitless; what is the use of even ten million preliminary rites?
